Many years ago my first wife and I lived in a terrible apartment complex. The SOP of the complex was whenever there was a water problem anywhere on the property, they'd shut off the main. No water for anybody. There were many times it lasted overnight. I learned quickly and acquired some 5 gallon water jugs from work. At least we could flush the toilet, make dinner, have something to drink, ect. It was the beginning of my prepping.

Fast forward a decade and I live in a suburban home. I still have water, but not as much as you might think. After a very interesting conversation with a retired FEMA worker I started spreading out my supply. All of your eggs in the basement isn't the best idea apparently.

I have a 55 gal barrel with a spout on the bottom in my basement. I keep half a dozen 5 gallon jugs in the garage. I've got a stack of water bottles in another room (about 6 cases). I also keep a case in all three vehicles. I take my camelback with me most days, just for convenience.

All said and done, not including toilets / water heater I've probably got close to a hundred gallons on hand. I know that's not enough to have a family of four survive for long, but it's better than nothing. I'm looking at investing in one of the rainwater collection systems (if you have one, please pm me and let me know what you think of it) but otherwise that's it. Now I do have three saving graces.

-Winter means snow, and most years there's lots of it

-There is a canal that runs most of the year about 300 yards from my house

-In the opposite direction about a 1/4 mile there is a golf course with a fairly large man made pond

I have made a decision recently to try and keep an eye out for other sources.

Do you guys hoard water? If so, why and how?
